column1: # Shelf — mention-sentiment labels for the keyboards category (M9).
# One line per (raw mention, product phrase): what does the text say about the product named by
# that phrase — positive, negative or neutral? Keyed by the phrase as written (normalized on
# whole tokens the way the matcher normalizes), not by a catalog product, so that the sample is
# not starved by how few catalog products these channels happen to discuss: sentiment is read the
# same way whether or not the product is in the seed list. Written by hand before any sentiment
# rule or lexicon existed, over the same real corpus as keyboards-mention-resolution.tsv.
# Policy. Positive when the author praises, recommends, or is glad about the product ("love it",
# "sounds so good", "just get a", "can't go wrong", "trust me"); negative when they disparage,
# regret, returned it, or it loses a comparison the author makes ("sucked", "TRASH", "returned it
# so fast", "a step up from the X" → X negative); neutral when the text only asks, requests a
# review, names it, or reports a fact ("is it worth it", "day 1 of asking", "on sale"). Questions
# are neutral even when leading ("what's wrong with Keychron?").
# Frozen 2026-09-17 before the first rule ran.
